The company, the mesh, the services and the people are fictional. The minutes or days each step takes and the effects of each decision are teaching simplifications for exam practice, not measured values.

brief.situation: You run the mesh at Glenmoor Energy, a fictional utility. The mesh is two minor versions behind and out of support. The upgrade must not interrupt the customer portal or the meter-reading APIs.
handover: Current control plane: istiod 1.22, installed in place, namespaces labeled istio-injection=enabled.
Upgrades are supported one minor version at a time.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the map shows each component and its status in words.
Move on a check-in at a time. A decision comes to you at each check-in; before the first, you can read the evidence.
At the end you write the record and a short reflection.

then.log: Check-in 2: 1.22 proxies reject part of the 1.24 configuration; the meters API's routes go missing and readings fail.
Check-in 3: restarted portal Pods start without sidecars and fail STRICT mTLS calls; the portal's login fails.
Check-in 4: the nightly billing export runs on the old revision's template; it gets no certificate and fails.

effects.log: Check-in 3: all three namespaces are on 1-23.

methodPrompt.title: In place or canary?
methodPrompt.context: An in-place upgrade replaces istiod for everyone at once. A revision-based upgrade runs the new istiod beside the old one.

choices.label: Install 1.23 as a separate revision (istioctl install with revision 1-23) beside 1.22, verify it, and plan 1.24 the same way afterwards
choices.feedback: A revision runs the new control plane alongside the old; workloads move when you choose, and you can move them back.

choices.label: Upgrade in place to 1.23 during a quiet hour
choices.feedback: Supported, but every proxy now talks to the new control plane at once and there is no side-by-side rollback.

choices.label: Go straight to 1.24 in place to save a step
choices.feedback: Skipping a minor version is unsupported; 1.22 proxies and a 1.24 control plane are outside the supported skew.

movePrompt.title: Move the workloads
movePrompt.context: Workloads pick a control plane at injection, when their Pods start.

choices.label: In billing first: replace istio-injection with istio.io/rev=1-23, restart its Deployments, check istioctl proxy-status shows them on 1-23 and traffic is healthy; then meters, then portal

effects.log: Namespaces move one by one, verified each time.

choices.feedback: The revision label picks the new control plane at the next restart; one namespace at a time keeps a bad step small.

choices.label: Relabel all three namespaces at once and let Pods pick up 1-23 as they restart naturally

effects.log: All namespaces relabeled; restarts happen over days.

choices.feedback: Nothing breaks now, but the mesh runs mixed for days and a problem shows up wherever a Pod happens to restart.

choices.label: Add istio.io/rev=1-23 but keep istio-injection=enabled too
choices.feedback: With both labels, injection is ambiguous; restarted Pods fail to get a sidecar or get the wrong one.

oldPrompt.title: Remove 1.22?
oldPrompt.context: proxy-status shows 41 proxies on 1-23 and one on 1.22: a CronJob's Pod that has not run since.

choices.label: Restart the CronJob's template so its next Pod injects 1-23, confirm proxy-status shows nothing on 1.22, then uninstall the 1.22 revision
choices.feedback: Remove the old revision only when no proxy depends on it.

choices.label: Keep 1.22 running indefinitely in case
choices.feedback: Nothing breaks, but an unsupported control plane stays in the cluster.

choices.label: Uninstall 1.22 now

effects.log: 1.22 is uninstalled with one proxy still on it.

choices.feedback: The CronJob's next Pod has no control plane for its revision and cannot get a certificate.

reflection.question: Write the change record: the upgrade method, how workloads moved and were verified, and when the old control plane was removed.

parts.label: Method
parts.criteria: A canary revision one minor version at a time.
parts.modelAnswer: We installed 1.23 as revision 1-23 beside 1.22; 1.24 follows the same way.

parts.label: Moving and removing
parts.criteria: One namespace at a time with istio.io/rev, verified by proxy-status; 1.22 removed at zero proxies.
parts.modelAnswer: Each namespace swapped istio-injection for istio.io/rev=1-23 and restarted, verified in proxy-status; 1.22 was removed when no proxy used it.

expertPath.text: Run the precheck and list the namespaces' injection labels.
Install 1.23 as a revision beside the old control plane.
Relabel and restart one namespace at a time, checking proxy-status and traffic.
Confirm no proxy is on the old revision, then uninstall it.

scoring.modelReasoning: A revision-based (canary) upgrade installs the new istiod beside the old one; namespaces choose a control plane with istio.io/rev, and Pods pick it up at their next injection, so moves are gradual and reversible. Upgrade one minor version at a time. Replace istio-injection with the revision label rather than adding both, verify each move with istioctl proxy-status and traffic, and remove the old revision only when no proxy still uses it.
